This is the R twin of the Python guide
[`distributions-for-actuaries-claim-size.md`](distributions-for-actuaries-claim-size.md).
It recomputes the worked examples and problem answers of chapters 2, 5 and 6 of
CAS Monograph 2, *Distributions for Actuaries* by David Bahnemann (2015). The
sections, examples and numbers are the same. The R package calls the same Rust
code as the Python package, so every number printed below equals the Python
guide's. Read that guide for the discussion of each result, and the monograph
for the derivations. The companion R guide,
[`distributions-for-actuaries-counts-aggregates.qmd`](distributions-for-actuaries-counts-aggregates.qmd),
covers chapters 3 and 4.

After each R chunk, a block shows the text that the chunk prints.
`R/prospicio/tests/test-guides.R` requires each chunk to print exactly that
text. The monograph's printed value is a literal in the code, printed next to
prospicio's. Example and problem numbers ("Ex 2.7", "P6.13") are the
monograph's. The Python guide minimizes with SciPy's Nelder–Mead. This guide
uses R's `optim()`. Both find the same minima to the printed digits.

## 1. Translating the parameters

| Monograph | Its formula | prospicio (R) |
|---|---|---|
| gamma (α, β), β a scale | mean αβ | `gamma_distribution(α, β)` |
| exponential β | mean β | `gamma_distribution(1, β)` |
| lognormal (μ, σ) | log X normal (μ, σ) | `lognormal(μ, σ)` |
| Weibull (β, δ) | F = 1 − exp(−(x/β)^δ) | `weibull_distribution(shape = δ, scale = β)` |
| Pareto (α, β), the "shifted" one used in all examples | F = 1 − (β/(x+β))^α, from 0 | `generalized_pareto(1/α, β/α)`, or `burr_distribution(α, 1, β)` |
| classical Pareto (γ, α) | F = 1 − (γ/x)^α, from γ | `pareto(γ, α)` |

The monograph's Pareto starts at zero (a Lomax). prospicio's `pareto()` is the
single-parameter Pareto above a threshold. The guide uses the helpers below
throughout. `limited_second_moment` builds E[X²; l] as `layer_variance +
layer^2` from a `truncated_distribution()` with no bounds. This gives layer
moments for any severity. The survival function of the lognormal is
`1 - cdf()`, and the standard deviation is `sqrt(variance())`.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(prospicio)

shifted_pareto <- function(alpha, beta) generalized_pareto(1 / alpha, beta / alpha)
surv <- function(sev, x) 1 - cdf(sev, x)
limited_second_moment <- function(sev, limit) {
  t <- truncated_distribution(sev)
  layer_variance(t, limit, 0) + layer(t, limit, 0)^2
}
layer_second_moment <- function(sev, limit, attachment) {
  t <- truncated_distribution(sev)
  layer_variance(t, limit, attachment) + layer(t, limit, attachment)^2
}
num <- function(x, digits = 0) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
show <- function(label, book, ours, digits = 0) {
  cat(sprintf("%-40s book %12s   prospicio %12s\n", label, num(book, digits), num(ours, digits)))
}
vec <- function(x, digits = 4) {
  paste0("[", paste(formatC(round(x, digits), format = "f", digits = digits), collapse = ", "), "]")
}

p <- shifted_pareto(2, 3000)
closed_form <- 3000 / (2 - 1) * (1 - 3000 / (8000 + 3000))
show("E[X; 8,000], Pareto (2; 3,000)", 2182, lev(p, 8000))
cat(sprintf("closed form %s, prospicio %s, Burr %s\n", num(closed_form, 2),
            num(lev(p, 8000), 2), num(lev(burr_distribution(2, 1, 3000), 8000), 2)))
```

```text
E[X; 8,000], Pareto (2; 3,000)           book        2,182   prospicio        2,182
closed form 2,181.82, prospicio 2,181.82, Burr 2,181.82
```

## 2. Limited expected values

```{r}
#| label: lev
x <- gamma_distribution(1, 250)
show("Ex 2.4  E[X; 400]", 199.53, lev(x, 400), 2)
show("Ex 2.4  E[X^2; 400]", 59384, limited_second_moment(x, 400))

x <- pareto(1000, 3)
show("P2.1   mean", 1500, mean(x))
show("P2.1   variance", 750000, variance(x))
show("P2.1   Pr{X > 2,000}", 0.1250, survival(x, 2000), 4)
show("P2.1   E[X; 2,000]", 1375, lev(x, 2000))

cases <- list(
  list("P2.17", lognormal(6.3210, 1.6000), c(556, 0.1461, 0.2108, 1023, 9689)),
  list("P2.19", shifted_pareto(3, 4000), c(1040, 0.1866, 0.3254, 1347, 6500))
)
for (case in cases) {
  name <- case[[1]]; x <- case[[2]]; book <- case[[3]]
  s3 <- surv(x, 3000)
  show(paste0(name, "  median"), book[1], quantile(x, 0.5))
  show(paste0(name, "  Pr{X > 3,000}"), book[2], s3, 4)
  show(paste0(name, "  Pr{1,000 < X <= 3,000}"), book[3], cdf(x, 3000) - cdf(x, 1000), 4)
  show(paste0(name, "  E[X; 3,000]"), book[4], lev(x, 3000))
  show(paste0(name, "  E[X | X > 3,000]"), book[5], 3000 + stop_loss(x, 3000) / s3)
}
```

P2.25: the mean is 1,000 and the standard deviation is 2,000. How many of 5,000
claims are more than 1,000 under each family?

```{r}
#| label: p225

             Pareto = shifted_pareto(8 / 3, 1000 * (8 / 3 - 1)))
book <- c(gamma = 1282, lognormal = 1315, Pareto = 1428)
for (name in names(fits)) {
  show(paste0("P2.25  claims > 1,000, ", name), book[[name]], 5000 * surv(fits[[name]], 1000))
}
```

## 3. Fitting grouped data

The method of moments for the gamma of Ex 2.7 uses the sample moments
M1 = 1,555 and M2 = 3,036,875 of the 200 claims of Ex 2.6. The printed scale
397.931 is a slip for 397.974. The monograph's tables use it. The table below
uses it too:

```{r}
#| label: ex27
M1 <- 1555; M2 <- 3036875
show("Ex 2.7  alpha", 3.907288, M1^2 / (M2 - M1^2), 6)
show("Ex 2.7  beta", 397.931, (M2 - M1^2) / M1, 3)

CUTS <- c(0, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000, Inf)
OBSERVED <- c(42, 61, 47, 26, 14, 10)
cell_probs <- function(sev, cuts) {
  F <- sapply(cuts, function(c) if (c == 0) 0 else if (is.infinite(c)) 1 else cdf(sev, c))
  diff(F)
}
chi_square <- function(sev, cuts = CUTS, observed = OBSERVED) {
  n <- sum(observed)
  e <- n * cell_probs(sev, cuts)
  sum((observed - e)^2 / e)
}
g <- gamma_distribution(3.907288, 397.931)
xs <- c(1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000)
cat("Ex 2.7  Pr{X > x}  book ", vec(c(0.7382, 0.4604, 0.2465, 0.1186, 0.0528)), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(surv(g, xs)), "\n")
cat("        E[X; x]    book ", vec(c(924, 1223, 1396, 1484, 1525), 0), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(sapply(xs, function(x) lev(g, x)), 0), "\n")
show("Ex 2.7  chi-square", 3.096, chi_square(g), 3)
```

```text

                   ours  [0.7382, 0.4604, 0.2465, 0.1186, 0.0528] 
        E[X; x]    book  [924, 1223, 1396, 1484, 1525] 
                   ours  [924, 1223, 1396, 1484, 1525]
```

Minimum chi-square, Ex 2.8 and P2.16. At the monograph's lognormal, the
statistic is 1.020, not the printed 1.828. The true minimum is lower:

```{r}
#| label: ex28
min_chi_square <- function(make, start, ...) {
  fit <- optim(start, function(p) chi_square(make(p[1], p[2]), ...), method = "Nelder-Mead",
               control = list(reltol = 1e-14, maxit = 4000))
  list(par = fit$par, value = fit$value)
}
ln <- lognormal(7.274670, 0.442525)
cat("Ex 2.8  Pr{X > x}  book ", vec(c(0.7965, 0.4653, 0.2305, 0.1072, 0.0491)), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(surv(ln, xs)), "\n")
cat("        E[X; x]    book ", vec(c(958, 1273, 1441, 1522, 1559), 0), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(sapply(xs, function(x) lev(ln, x)), 0), "\n")
show("Ex 2.8  chi-square at its fit", 1.828, chi_square(ln), 3)
f <- min_chi_square(function(m, s) lognormal(m, abs(s)), c(7.2, 0.5))
cat(sprintf("        smallest chi-square %.3f at (%.4f, %.4f)\n", f$value, f$par[1], abs(f$par[2])))
f <- min_chi_square(function(a, b) gamma_distribution(abs(a), abs(b)), c(4, 400))
show("P2.16  gamma by min chi-square: a", 4.7432, abs(f$par[1]), 4)
show("P2.16  b", 337.31, abs(f$par[2]), 2)
```

```text
Ex 2.8  Pr{X > x}  book  [0.7965, 0.4653, 0.2305, 0.1072, 0.0491] 
                   ours  [0.7965, 0.4653, 0.2305, 0.1072, 0.0491] 
        E[X; x]    book  [958, 1273, 1441, 1522, 1559] 
                   ours  [958, 1273, 1441, 1522, 1559] 
Ex 2.8  chi-square at its fit            book        1.828   prospicio        1.020
        smallest chi-square 0.614 at (7.2857, 0.4570)
P2.16  gamma by min chi-square: a        book       4.7432   prospicio       4.7432
```


## 4. Censored and truncated data

Minimum limited-mean distance for the censored samples of Ex 2.10 and P2.39:

```{r}
#| label: censored
min_distance <- function(sizes, empirical, start) {
  distance <- function(p) {
    ln <- lognormal(p[1], abs(p[2]))
    sum((sapply(sizes, function(x) lev(ln, x)) - empirical)^2)
  }
  fit <- optim(start, distance, method = "Nelder-Mead", control = list(reltol = 1e-14, maxit = 4000))
  c(fit$par[1], abs(fit$par[2]))
}
sizes <- c(1000, 5000, 10000, 25000, 50000, 100000, 200000, 300000)
below <- c(729, 1096, 1208, 1326, 1391, 1440, 1468, 1500)
total_below <- c(225138, 1102272, 1918947, 3752091, 6007543, 9234739, 13100561, 22343455)
emp <- (total_below + sizes * (1500 - below)) / 1500
f <- min_distance(sizes, emp, c(7, 2.5))
show("Ex 2.10 mu", 6.9852, f[1], 4)
show("Ex 2.10 sigma", 2.5850, f[2], 4)
cat("Ex 2.10 E[X; x] book ", vec(c(648, 2091, 3239, 5410, 7580, 10168, 13069, 14850), 0), "\n")
cat("            prospicio", vec(sapply(sizes, function(x) lev(lognormal(f[1], f[2]), x)), 0), "\n")

sizes <- c(10000, 20000, 30000, 40000, 50000, 60000, 80000, 100000)
counts <- c(78, 27, 21, 15, 12, 10, 8, 7)          # 22 more at the 100,000 limit
mids <- c(5000, 15000, 25000, 35000, 45000, 55000, 70000, 90000)
emp <- (cumsum(counts * mids) + sizes * (200 - cumsum(counts))) / 200
f <- min_distance(sizes, emp, c(9.7, 1.4))
show("P2.39 mu", 9.778102, f[1], 4)
show("P2.39 sigma", 1.444776, f[2], 4)
```

```text
Ex 2.10 mu                               book       6.9852   prospicio       6.9852
Ex 2.10 sigma                            book       2.5850   prospicio       2.5850
Ex 2.10 E[X; x] book  [648, 2091, 3239, 5410, 7580, 10168, 13069, 14850] 
            prospicio [648, 2091, 3239, 5410, 7580, 10168, 13069, 14850] 
P2.39 mu                                 book       9.7781   prospicio       9.7781
P2.39 sigma                              book       1.4448   prospicio       1.4448
```

Truncation from below (Ex 2.11, a 1,000 deductible and a 200,000 limit) and from
above (P2.43), with `truncated_distribution()`:

```{r}
#| label: truncated
cuts <- c(1000, 5000, 10000, 25000, 50000, 75000, 100000, 125000, 150000, 175000, 200000, Inf)
observed <- c(367, 112, 118, 65, 36, 13, 10, 8, 6, 4, 31)
f <- min_chi_square(function(m, s) truncated_distribution(lognormal(m, abs(s)), lower = 1000),
                    c(6.7, 2.7), cuts = cuts, observed = observed)
show("Ex 2.11 mu", 6.6916, f$par[1], 4)
show("Ex 2.11 sigma", 2.6965, abs(f$par[2]), 4)
show("Ex 2.11 chi-square", 4.691, f$value, 3)
fitted <- truncated_distribution(lognormal(f$par[1], abs(f$par[2])), lower = 1000)
cat("Ex 2.11 expected book ", vec(c(360, 122, 121, 63, 27, 16, 10, 7, 5, 4, 34), 0), "\n")
cat("            prospicio ", vec(770 * cell_probs(fitted, cuts), 0), "\n")

cuts <- 5000 * (0:10)
observed <- c(104, 120, 81, 54, 45, 32, 26, 18, 12, 8)
f <- min_chi_square(function(m, s) truncated_distribution(lognormal(m, abs(s)), upper = 50000),
                    c(9.5, 1.1), cuts = cuts, observed = observed)
show("P2.43 mu", 9.495111, f$par[1], 4)
show("P2.43 sigma", 1.084180, abs(f$par[2]), 4)
```

```text
Ex 2.11 mu                               book       6.6916   prospicio       6.6916
Ex 2.11 sigma                            book       2.6965   prospicio       2.6965
Ex 2.11 chi-square                       book        4.691   prospicio        4.691
Ex 2.11 expected book  [360, 122, 121, 63, 27, 16, 10, 7, 5, 4, 34] 
            prospicio  [360, 122, 121, 63, 27, 16, 10, 7, 5, 4, 34] 
P2.43 mu                                 book       9.4951   prospicio       9.4951
P2.43 sigma                              book       1.0842   prospicio       1.0842
```

`severity_fit()` fits individual claims by maximum likelihood. The deductible is
a reporting threshold and the limit is censoring. The 20,000 draws are the same
as in the Python guide (both guides share the generator):

```{r}
#| label: fit
truth <- lognormal(6.6916, 2.6965)
ground_up <- draws(truth, 20000, seed = 2)
kept <- ground_up[ground_up > 1000]
recorded <- pmin(kept, 200000)
at_limit <- kept >= 200000
cat(sprintf("%s of 20,000 claims recorded, %d at the limit\n", num(length(kept)), sum(at_limit)))
fits <- list(
  "ignoring both" = severity_fit("lognormal", recorded),
  "censoring only" = severity_fit("lognormal", recorded, censored = at_limit),
  "truncation and censoring" = severity_fit("lognormal", recorded, censored = at_limit,
                                            reporting_thresholds = rep(1000, length(kept)))
)
for (label in names(fits)) {
  f <- fits[[label]]
  cat(sprintf("%-25s mu %5.2f (se %.2f)  sigma %4.2f\n", label, f$parameters[["meanlog"]],
              f$standard_errors[["meanlog"]], f$parameters[["sdlog"]]))
}
```

```text
9,551 of 20,000 claims recorded, 415 at the limit
ignoring both             mu  8.94 (se 0.01)  sigma 1.46
censoring only            mu  8.96 (se 0.02)  sigma 1.52
truncation and censoring  mu  6.76 (se 0.15)  sigma 2.67
```

## 5. Inflation and claim size

```{r}
#| label: inflation
p <- shifted_pareto(2, 3000)
base <- lev(p, 8000)
up <- lev(shifted_pareto(2, 3000 * 1.10), 8000)
down <- 0.95 * lev(p, 8000 / 0.95)
show("Ex 2.15 E[X; 8,000]", 2182, base)
show("        after +10%", 2336, up)
show("        effective rate, %", 7.1, 100 * (up / base - 1), 1)
show("        after -5%", 2101, down)
show("        effective rate, %", -3.7, 100 * (down / base - 1), 1)

before <- lognormal(7.2, 0.476)
after <- lognormal(1.0183 * 7.2 + log(0.96), 1.0183 * 0.476)
show("Ex 2.16 mean before", 1500, mean(before))
show("        mean after", 1650, mean(after))
cat(sprintf("        inflation of a claim of 1,000: %.2f%%, of 5,000: %.2f%%\n",
            100 * (0.96 * 1000^0.0183 - 1), 100 * (0.96 * 5000^0.0183 - 1)))
```

```text
Ex 2.15 E[X; 8,000]                      book        2,182   prospicio        2,182
        after +10%                       book        2,336   prospicio        2,336
        effective rate, %                book          7.1   prospicio          7.1
        after -5%                        book        2,101   prospicio        2,101
        effective rate, %                book         -3.7   prospicio         -3.7
Ex 2.16 mean before                      book        1,500   prospicio        1,500
        mean after                       book        1,650   prospicio        1,650
        inflation of a claim of 1,000: 8.94%, of 5,000: 12.19%
```

## 6. Excess claims and layers

```{r}
#| label: excess
cases <- list(
  list("uniform [0; 4,000]", 500, beta_distribution(1, 1, 4000)),
  list("gamma (2; 1,000)", 1250, gamma_distribution(2, 1000)),
  list("exponential 2,000", 2000, gamma_distribution(1, 2000)),
  list("Pareto (3; 4,000)", 3500, shifted_pareto(3, 4000)),
  list("lognormal (5.9809; 1.8)", 8518, lognormal(5.9809, 1.8))
)
for (case in cases) {
  show(paste0("P5.2  e(3,000), ", case[[1]]), case[[2]], stop_loss(case[[3]], 3000) / surv(case[[3]], 3000))
}
alpha <- 1 + 1 / 0.257335
beta <- 1208.50 * (alpha - 1)
show("Ex 5.4  alpha", 4.88599, alpha, 5)
show("Ex 5.4  beta", 4696.22, beta, 2)
p <- shifted_pareto(alpha, beta)
xs <- c(500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000)
cat("Ex 5.4  F(x)     book ", vec(c(0.3900, 0.6106, 0.8233, 0.9711, 0.9962)), "\n")
cat("                 ours ", vec(cdf(p, xs)), "\n")
cat("        E[X; x]  book ", vec(c(393, 638, 904, 1136, 1194), 0), "\n")
cat("                 ours ", vec(sapply(xs, function(x) lev(p, x)), 0), "\n")

p <- shifted_pareto(2, 3000)
show("Ex 5.7  E[X; 5,000]", 1875, lev(p, 5000))
show("        E[X; 9,000]", 2250, lev(p, 9000))
show("        layer mean per excess claim", 2667, layer(p, 4000, 5000) / survival(p, 5000))
show("        as Pareto (2; 8,000) at 4,000", 2667, lev(shifted_pareto(2, 8000), 4000))
```

Coefficients of variation of the lognormal (5.9809; 1.8) and its layers (Ex 5.8,
P5.10). The monograph's differences of rounded limited means cause the
differences in the third and fourth figures:

```{r}
#| label: ex58
ln <- lognormal(5.9809, 1.8)
s3 <- surv(ln, 3000)
layer_mean <- layer(ln, 5000, 3000) / s3
layer_m2 <- layer_second_moment(ln, 5000, 3000) / s3
cv_limited <- function(l) sqrt(limited_second_moment(ln, l) - lev(ln, l)^2) / lev(ln, l)
show("Ex 5.8  F(3,000)", 0.869761, cdf(ln, 3000), 6)
show("        E[X; 3,000]", 891, lev(ln, 3000))
show("        E[X^2; 3,000]", 1853050, limited_second_moment(ln, 3000))
show("        E[X^2; 8,000]", 5774970, limited_second_moment(ln, 8000))
show("        CV[X]", 4.9531, sqrt(variance(ln)) / mean(ln), 4)
show("        E[X_3K], the excess mean", 8515, stop_loss(ln, 3000) / s3)
show("        CV of the layer 5K xs 3K", 0.6452, sqrt(layer_m2 - layer_mean^2) / layer_mean, 4)
show("P5.10   CV[X; 3,000]", 1.1551, cv_limited(3000), 4)
show("P5.10   CV[X; 8,000]", 1.5959, cv_limited(8000), 4)
m <- (1276 - 891) / 0.130239
m2 <- (5774970 - 1853050 - 2 * 3000 * (1276 - 891)) / 0.130239
cat(sprintf("        layer CV from the printed, rounded inputs: %.4f\n", sqrt(m2 - m * m) / m))
```

P5.12's three layers of a policy with a 100 deductible and a 3,000 limit,
Pareto (3; 5,000), 5 ground-up claims:

```{r}
#| label: p512
p <- shifted_pareto(3, 5000)
layers <- list(list("[0; 100]", 0, 100, c(1.0000, 97.08, 485)),
               list("(100; 3,000]", 100, 2900, c(0.9423, 1513.66, 7132)),
               list("(3,000; inf)", 3000, Inf, c(0.2441, 4000.00, 4883)))
total <- 0
for (L in layers) {
  reach <- survival(p, L[[2]])
  loss <- if (is.infinite(L[[3]])) stop_loss(p, L[[2]]) else layer(p, L[[3]], L[[2]])
  total <- total + 5 * loss
  show(paste("P5.12", L[[1]], "share reaching"), L[[4]][1], reach, 4)
  show(paste("P5.12", L[[1]], "severity"), L[[4]][2], loss / reach, 2)
  show(paste("P5.12", L[[1]], "expected loss"), L[[4]][3], 5 * loss)
}
show("P5.12 total = 5 x mean", 12500, total)
for (case in list(list("Ex 5.3", 43, c(8.67593, 1.18109), 300, 1500),
                  list("P5.23", 125, c(7.960294, 1.428801), 1000, 500))) {
  f <- cdf(lognormal(case[[3]][1], case[[3]][2]), case[[5]])
  show(paste(case[[1]], "claims hidden by the deductible"), case[[2]], case[[4]] * f / (1 - f))
}
```

## 7. Inflation above an attachment: the leveraging effect

```{r}
#| label: leverage
p <- shifted_pareto(2, 3000); t <- 1.10
e0 <- stop_loss(p, 5000) / survival(p, 5000)
e1 <- t * stop_loss(p, 5000 / t) / survival(p, 5000 / t)
show("Ex 5.10 e(5,000)", 8000, e0)
show("        e(5,000) after inflation", 8300, e1)
show("        excess severity trend, %", 3.75, 100 * (e1 / e0 - 1), 2)
layer0 <- layer(p, 4000, 5000) / survival(p, 5000)
layer1 <- t * layer(p, 4000 / t, 5000 / t) / survival(p, 5000 / t)
show("        layer 4K xs 5K severity, trended", 2701, layer1)
show("        layer severity trend, %", 1.27, 100 * (layer1 / layer0 - 1), 2)
count <- survival(p, 5000 / t) / survival(p, 5000)
show("Ex 5.11 excess count factor", 1.1241, count, 4)
show("Ex 5.12 excess count trend, %", 18.03, 100 * (1.05 * count - 1), 2)
show("        excess loss trend, %", 22.46, 100 * (1.05 * count * e1 / e0 - 1), 2)
show("        of which from claim size, %", 16.6, 100 * (count * e1 / e0 - 1), 1)

x <- gamma_distribution(1, 1000)
s <- survival(x, 1000)
lm <- layer(x, 2000, 1000) / s
show("P5.1  layer mean per excess claim", 865, lm)
show("      its variance", 440343, layer_second_moment(x, 2000, 1000) / s - lm^2)
show("      excess claims, of 20", 7.4, 20 * s, 1)
sev <- t * layer(x, 2000 / t, 1000 / t) / survival(x, 1000 / t) / lm - 1
cnt <- survival(x, 1000 / t) / s - 1
show("      severity trend, %", 6.6, 100 * sev, 1)
show("      count trend, %", 9.5, 100 * cnt, 1)
show("      loss trend, %", 16.7, 100 * ((1 + sev) * (1 + cnt) - 1), 1)
ln <- lognormal(5.9809, 1.8)
for (case in list(c(3000, 8.9), c(8000, 11.5))) {
  show(sprintf("P5.21 count trend above %s, %%", num(case[1])), case[2],
       100 * (surv(ln, case[1] / t) / surv(ln, case[1]) - 1), 1)
}
for (case in list(c(2000, 9.5), c(5000, 10.2))) {
  show(sprintf("P5.22 loss trend, layer to %s, %%", num(3000 + case[1])), case[2],
       100 * (t * layer(ln, case[1] / t, 3000 / t) / layer(ln, case[1], 3000) - 1), 1)
}
show("Ex 5.13 E[S]", 5775, 15 * layer(ln, 5000, 3000))
show("        Var[S]", 24178800, 15 * layer_second_moment(ln, 5000, 3000))
show("        expected layer claims", 1.9536, 15 * surv(ln, 3000), 4)
```

## 9. Risk loads

```{r}
#| label: risk-load
sd_load <- function(sev, l, k, delta) k * sqrt(limited_second_moment(sev, l) + delta * lev(sev, l)^2)
var_load <- function(sev, l, k, delta) k * (limited_second_moment(sev, l) + delta * lev(sev, l)^2)
loaded_ilf <- function(sev, l, base, k, delta, load = sd_load, u = 0.2) {
  premium <- function(x) (1 + u) * lev(sev, x) + load(sev, x, k, delta)
  premium(l) / premium(base)
}
cat("Ex 6.5  rho(l)     book ", vec(c(627, 1473, 2013, 2663, 3090, 3410, 3668), 0), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(sapply(limits, function(l) sd_load(ln, l, 0.0277, 0)), 0), "\n")
loaded <- sapply(limits, function(l) loaded_ilf(ln, l, b, 0.0277, 0))
cat("        loaded I   book ", vec(c(1.0, 1.5770, 1.8074, 2.0128, 2.1197, 2.1897, 2.2407)), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(loaded), "\n")
mix <- c(0.15, 0.10, 0.30, 0.20, 0.10, 0.10, 0.05)
plain <- sum(mix * sapply(limits, function(l) ilf(ln, l, b)))
risky <- sum(mix * loaded)
show("        average I, no load", 1.6938, plain, 4)
show("        average I, loaded", 1.7955, risky, 4)
show("        the load's effect, %", 6.0, 100 * (risky / plain - 1), 1)

p <- shifted_pareto(3, 6000)
limits4 <- c(1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 7500, 10000)
cat("P6.8   I, no load  book ", vec(c(1.0, 1.6490, 2.0940, 2.4123, 2.6478, 3.0247, 3.2392)), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(sapply(limits4, function(l) ilf(p, l, 1000))), "\n")
cat("       I, loaded   book ", vec(c(1.0, 1.6787, 2.1645, 2.5267, 2.8055, 3.2805, 3.5759)), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(sapply(limits4, function(l) loaded_ilf(p, l, 1000, 0.5, 0.1))), "\n")
p <- shifted_pareto(0.78, 100)
f <- sapply((1:10) * 1e6, function(l) loaded_ilf(p, l, 1e6, 5e-7, 0, load = var_load, u = 0))
cat("P6.10  I(l)        book ", vec(c(1.0, 1.3858, 1.7458, 2.1014, 2.4585, 2.8194, 3.1849,
                                       3.5553, 3.9309, 3.4114)), "\n")
cat("                   ours ", vec(f), "\n")
cat("       layer factor book ", vec(c(0.3556, 0.3571, 0.3609, 0.3655, 0.3705, 0.3755, 0.3806)), "\n")
```

## 10. Deductibles

```{r}
#| label: deductibles
base <- lev(ln, b)
deds <- c(1000, 2000, 3000, 4000, 5000, 10000)
dlev <- sapply(deds, function(d) lev(ln, d))
straight <- dlev / base
franchise <- (dlev - deds * surv(ln, deds)) / base
diminishing <- (dlev - deds * (sapply(deds + 1000, function(d) lev(ln, d)) - dlev) / 1000) / base
cat("Ex 6.7  C(d) straight     book ", vec(c(0.0741, 0.1249, 0.1661, 0.2016, 0.2328, 0.3534)), "\n")
cat("                          ours ", vec(straight), "\n")
cat("        frequency x 10^6  book ", vec(c(258, 201, 169, 147, 132, 89), 0), "\n")
cat("                          ours ", vec(1e6 * 0.0005 * surv(ln, deds), 0), "\n")
cat("        pure premium      book ", vec(c(4.942, 4.671, 4.451, 4.262, 4.095, 3.451), 3), "\n")
cat("                          ours ", vec(0.0005 * 1.2 * (base - dlev), 3), "\n")
cat("Ex 6.8  C(d) franchise    book ", vec(c(0.0162, 0.0347, 0.0523, 0.0690, 0.0846, 0.1528)), "\n")
cat("                          ours ", vec(franchise), "\n")
cat("Ex 6.9  C(d) diminishing  book ", vec(c(0.0233, 0.0424, 0.0599, 0.0766, 0.0917)), "\n")
cat("                          ours ", vec(diminishing[1:5]), "\n")
show("Ex 6.7  1M limit, 2,000 deductible", 5527,
     basic_u * (loaded_ilf(ln, 1e6, b, 0.0277, 0) - straight[2]))
cat(sprintf("prospicio's loss_elimination_ratio(2,000) = E[X; 2,000] / E[X] = %.4f\n",
            loss_elimination_ratio(ln, 2000)))

losses <- c(1000, 1550, 1700, 2200, 2500, 3000, 5200, 9000, 11000, 12500, 15000, 19800)
for (case in list(list("P6.13", 20000, c(62200, 0.2635, 80200, 0.0503)),
                  list("P6.14", 12000, c(50900, 0.3973, 68900, 0.1841)))) {
  capped <- pmin(losses, case[[2]])
  paid_straight <- sum(pmax(capped - 2000, 0))
  paid_franchise <- sum(capped[losses > 2000])
  bk <- case[[3]]
  show(paste(case[[1]], "straight: insurer pays"), bk[1], paid_straight)
  show(paste(case[[1]], "straight: LER"), bk[2], 1 - paid_straight / sum(losses), 4)
  show(paste(case[[1]], "franchise: insurer pays"), bk[3], paid_franchise)
  show(paste(case[[1]], "franchise: LER"), bk[4], 1 - paid_franchise / sum(losses), 4)
}
```

```{r}
cat("                        ours ", vec(0.0005 * (base - dlev + e * surv(ln, deds)), 3), "\n")
cat("       franchise C(d)   book ", vec(c(0.0411, 0.0647, 0.0848, 0.1028, 0.1193, 0.1884)), "\n")
cat("                        ours ", vec((dlev - deds * surv(ln, deds) + e * cdf(ln, deds)) / (base + e)), "\n")

p <- shifted_pareto(3, 10000)
deds2 <- c(0, 250, 500, 750, 1000)
plev <- sapply(deds2, function(d) lev(p, d))
base2 <- lev(p, 5000) + 250
cat("P6.17  straight C(d)    book ", vec(c(0.0, 0.0855, 0.1648, 0.2385, 0.3071)), "\n")
cat("                        ours ", vec((plev + 250 * cdf(p, deds2)) / base2), "\n")
cat("       pure premium     book ", vec(c(15.139, 13.845, 12.644, 11.528, 10.489), 3), "\n")
cat("                        ours ", vec(0.005 * (base2 - plev - 250 * cdf(p, deds2)), 3), "\n")
cat("       franchise C(d)   book ", vec(c(0.0088, 0.0221, 0.0391, 0.0590)), "\n")
cat("                        ours ", vec(((plev - deds2 * survival(p, deds2) + 250 * cdf(p, deds2)) / base2)[-1]), "\n")

d5 <- deds[1:5]
cat("P6.21  claims removed   book ", vec(c(242, 299, 331, 353, 368), 0), "\n")
cat("                        ours ", vec(500 * cdf(ln, d5), 0), "\n")
cat("       after inflation  book ", vec(c(234, 292, 324, 346, 362), 0), "\n")
cat("                        ours ", vec(500 * cdf(ln, d5 / 1.1), 0), "\n")
cat("       share removed, % book ", vec(c(7.1, 12.0, 16.1, 19.5, 22.6), 1), "\n")
cat("                        ours ", vec(100 * sapply(d5, function(d) lev(ln, d / 1.1)) / lev(ln, b / 1.1), 1), "\n")

pure_premium <- function(sev, top, d, e, phi = 0.25) {
  capped <- if (is.null(top)) mean(sev) else lev(sev, top)
  phi * (capped - lev(sev, d) + surv(sev, d) * e)
}
now <- shifted_pareto(2, 8000); later <- shifted_pareto(2, 8400)
for (case in list(list(NULL, c(1893, 1994, 5.3), 0, "no limit"),
                  list(5000, c(662.7, 677.3, 2.2), 1, "5,000 limit"))) {
  p0 <- pure_premium(now, case[[1]], 500, 50)
  p1 <- pure_premium(later, case[[1]], 500, 52.5)
  show(paste0("Ex 6.10 ", case[[4]], ": pure premium"), case[[2]][1], p0, case[[3]])
  show("        after 5% inflation", case[[2]][2], p1, case[[3]])
  show("        effective trend, %", case[[2]][3], 100 * (p1 / p0 - 1), 1)
}
```

## 11. What agreed and what did not

The comparisons are the same as in section 11 of the Python guide, with the same
numbers. They cover rounding carried into differences, misprints and
spreadsheet solver results. The reasons for each disagreement are in that
section.
